data.topic: Build-readiness review of the eleven planned phases of packet specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build (001-activity-and-actor, 002-routine-layer, 003-terminal-screen, 004-computer-exposure, 005-memory, 006-approval-grants, 007-per-bot-apps, 008-vault, 009-skills, 010-conversations, 011-messaging-channels). Each phase has spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md and acceptance-criteria.md. They were written in parallel, each alone, and nobody has checked them against the built runtime or against each other. This is a review of plans, not new design research. Evidence (read-only): the phase docs; the built skilled-bots runtime (.skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/runtime/lib/, .skilled/bin/bots.cjs, .skilled/skills/system-skilled-bots/scripts/bot-check.cjs, runtime/tests/); the parity research synthesis specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md; the reference repos under specs/system-skilled-bots/context/ (OpenBot-main, OpenMausBot-main, rakazo-main, openhuman-main, OpenGhost-main, hermes-muse-main, turnstone-main, buzz-main, tinychannels-main). Four angles: 1. Plan versus runtime: do the files, functions, records, fields and verbs each plan names exist with the shapes it assumes, and are its test and verify commands runnable here? 2. Cross-phase consistency: do the phases agree on shared records (by: actor, grants, operators.json, conversation JSONL, memory files, state-root layout, HonoredPosture fields, bots --json output read by the terminal screen and the channels), and are the build order and dependencies sound? 3. Parity gaps and overbuild: for a small team, what is still missing after all eleven phases, and what do the plans build that is not needed or duplicates another phase or the runtime? 4. Security and failure modes: secret leakage, token storage, spoofed chat users, who may approve, restarts, lost or duplicated messages and answers, concurrent approvals from terminal and chat, prompt injection through memory, skills or chat, routine until and fatigue edge cases. Every finding names the phase, the doc and line, the evidence with [SOURCE: path:line], a severity (P0 blocks the build, P1 wrong or missing, P2 polish) and the exact spec edit that fixes it. End with findings grouped by phase and ranked, plus a cross-phase conflict list.
